stage0_note: Unusually for a comparison record, the ledger is good: eight papers, seven of them human trials of the two compounds together or separately, including the trial whose four arms make this a genuine head-to-head. The drafted claims describe the combination rather than the comparison, so the guide draws the comparison out of the trial arms.

serp_2026-09-24.note: A clinical results set: the New England Journal paper second, PubMed fifth, the Lancet seventh, and specialist trade press filling the rest. No clinic, no telehealth service and no vendor ranks.

demand_findings: The comparison itself is small at 101, and the cluster around it is not: 'cagrilintide dosage' draws 2,136 at KD 0 and belongs to that compound's own written record, where it is redirected. What remains for this page is about 1,200, led by community discussion at 712 and the monotherapy questions.
h1: Cagrilintide vs semaglutide: one trial gave each of them alone, and semaglutide won
dek: These two are usually discussed as a combination. The trial that made the combination famous also randomised people to each drug by itself, which makes this one of the few comparisons on this site with a direct answer: 16.1 per cent against 11.8 per cent, in the same study, over the same 68 weeks.

information_gain: The only page to answer this comparison with the arms that exist rather than across trials. REDEFINE 1 randomised 3,417 adults to the combination, to semaglutide 2.4 mg alone, to cagrilintide 2.4 mg alone, or to placebo, and the two monotherapy arms are a direct comparison at the same dose over the same 68 weeks: semaglutide 16.1 per cent, cagrilintide 11.8 per cent. The only page to set that beside cagrilintide's own monotherapy evidence, a 2026 meta-analysis putting it at about 6 per cent against placebo, and to draw the conclusion that follows: cagrilintide is the addition in this pairing rather than the base, which is how the development programme treats it and not how the market discusses it. And the only page to note that this is a rare clean comparison, because both were given at 2.4 mg once weekly in the same trial, so none of the usual cross-trial caveats apply.
serp_format_rewarded: Primary literature. The New England Journal ranks second and the Lancet seventh; no commercial page ranks at all. A page that reads the trial arms correctly is the only kind that belongs here.
open_actions: The REDEFINE 1 arm-level figures are the manufacturer's announced numbers under the trial-product estimand; the published paper reports the combination under a different estimand. Both are given, cited editorially with pending_source, as on the CagriSema page.
Cagrilintide's own record carries its dose and side-effect detail and takes the 2,136-search dosage cluster.
